evals.prompt:
I already know the workflows I want to automate. Here are three:

1. Weekly client status reports — every Friday I pull data from 3 different project management tools (Asana, Harvest, and Slack), compile time tracking, milestone updates, and blockers into a Google Doc for each of my 8 clients. Takes me about 3 hours.

2. New client onboarding — when we sign a new client, I have to create their Asana project from a template, set up a Slack channel, add them to Harvest, send a welcome email with next steps, and schedule the kickoff call. Lots of copy-paste and I always forget at least one step.

3. Invoice reconciliation — at month end I cross-reference Harvest time entries against Asana task completion and our contract rates to make sure we're billing accurately. Usually takes half a day and I've caught errors both ways.

I'm a freelance operations consultant working solo. Can you analyze these?
evals.expected_output: Should take the fast path (skip interview), infer individual lens, produce a full opportunity report with 3 detailed cards grouped by process, a summary table with Size, and the value lever appendix, list every candidate in a catalog confirmation (no registry, so they stay in the report), and write to framework/ai-opportunity-report.md.
expectations: The response infers the individual lens without asking the user to choose
The response does NOT ask discovery interview questions since the user provided pre-identified workflows
An output file is written to framework/ai-opportunity-report.md
The report contains a Summary Table with all 3 opportunities
Each opportunity card includes a Value lever line naming one of Streamline, Automate, Accelerate, or Create value
The report names no tool, connector, or platform the user did not mention
The report includes the Value Lever Definitions appendix
The report groups opportunity cards by process, and each card has a Size line

The response does NOT ask the user to pick workflow candidates; it shows a catalog confirmation listing each workflow's name and one-line description, and keeps every candidate (in the report, since the workspace has no registry)

evals.prompt: I'm a marketing manager at a B2B SaaS company (about 50 employees). I manage a team of 3 — one content writer, one designer, and one social media person. My days are mostly spent in meetings, reviewing content drafts, pulling campaign performance data from HubSpot and Google Analytics, and writing the monthly board deck slides about marketing pipeline contribution. I feel like I'm drowning in busywork and not doing enough strategic thinking. Where can AI help me?
evals.expected_output: Should take the standard path, summarize what it knows from the conversation, ask permission before reading any history, select individual lens (or ask), conduct a brief interview to probe for more detail, then produce the opportunity report. Should ask one question at a time.
expectations: The first response summarizes what it already knows about the user before asking questions
Questions are asked one at a time, not as a list
The response selects or asks about the individual vs organizational lens
The report identifies at least 3 concrete opportunities
Opportunities are specific to the user's described role (not generic AI advice)
The report contains the required Report Header with role, date, lens, and count
The report does not rank opportunities: no Top Recommendations section, no top recommendation, no priority or impact rating

After the report, the response shows a catalog confirmation listing each workflow's name and one-line description, grouped by process or area of work, and keeps every candidate (in the report, since the workspace has no registry); it does not ask the user to pick which to build
The response never reads saved memory or past chats for opportunities without first asking permission, and never quotes a past chat; with no history to read, it skips that step
No question shows the literal "Ask:" label

evals.prompt:
I'm the founder and CEO of a 15-person SaaS startup that sells project management software to construction companies. Our top priority this quarter is reducing churn — we're at 8% monthly and need to get to 4%. The main processes I'm worried about are:
- Customer onboarding (takes 3 weeks, involves sales handoff to CS, product setup, training)
- Support ticket handling (we get ~200/week, 3 CS reps, avg resolution is 48 hours)
- Renewal/expansion conversations (CS manager handles these manually, no system)

Where can AI help us hit our churn target?
evals.expected_output: Should infer organizational lens from the business-objective framing. Should either fast-path or do a brief interview. Report should include organizational-only fields (Business Objective, Stakeholders, Success Metrics) on each card. All opportunities should tie back to the churn reduction objective.
expectations: The response infers the organizational lens based on the business-objective framing
Opportunities are tied to the stated churn reduction objective
Each opportunity card includes Business Objective, Stakeholders, and Success Metrics fields
The report identifies at least 3 concrete opportunities
The report contains the required Summary Table format
Each card has a Size line, in the user's own numbers or "Not sized yet"

After the report, the response shows a catalog confirmation listing each workflow's name and one-line description, grouped by process or area of work, and keeps every candidate (in the report, since the workspace has no registry); it does not ask the user to pick which to build
Recommendations are specific to the construction SaaS context, not generic

evals.prompt: Run the analyze skill. (Workspace: a registry for a small consulting firm with 6 processes. When asked, the user allows the history check; their past chats show they ask for proposal drafts often and that their 'Newsletter Repurposer' skill turns each newsletter issue into LinkedIn posts, which works well. The user keeps both, walks only 'Client Onboarding', then says 'stop here for now'.)
evals.expected_output: Asks permission before reading history, shows the two items as opportunities, registers the Newsletter Repurposer work as in production with the skill named under # Skills, walks one process, then writes a report with a Not looked at yet row and closes with an offer to pick up the rest.
expectations: The response asks permission before reading saved memory or past chats
The newsletter repurposing work is registered with status: in-production, with Newsletter Repurposer under # Skills, and is not in the backlog
No size guess is asked for the work that already runs
The report header has a Not looked at yet row listing the five processes not walked
The close says how many processes were looked at and how to pick up the rest
No question shows the literal "Ask:" label
